solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Releases soccer team goals

blocks.note: Man U, short for Manchester United football club
aims or purposes one sets out to achieve

explanation.surface: A football club announces its signings and goals, as in a press release.
explanation.definitionFit: Manumission is the formal freeing of a slave, so the plural noun means acts of liberation or setting free.

clue.text: Crustacean mum cooked isn’t a tiny one

indicators.note: food that is cooked is prepared and changed, so the following word is rearranged

blocks.note: a familiar word for mother
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a shrimp is slang for a very small person

explanation.surface: Mum cooks a crustacean and complains that it is not a small one.
explanation.walkthrough: MA + an anagram of ISNT gives MANTIS, then SHRIMP; 'a tiny one' is a person, not a prawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The mantis shrimp is a marine stomatopod, famous for its powerful smashing claws and complex eyes.

clue.text: Smart person caught out in festival

indicators.note: the cricket abbreviation for caught is put out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a smart alec is a know-all

explanation.surface: A clever person is caught out at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the scorecard abbreviation for caught. ALE as a festival is an old use, as in church-ale or bride-ale.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English an ale was a village merrymaking or feast where ale was drunk, hence a festive gathering.

clue.text: Source of poison mostly unusual for number in college

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost
one thing given in exchange for another means a swap inside the word

blocks.note: rare, missing its final letter
N is the abbreviation for number
short for university

explanation.surface: Something odd about how many students a college has may be the root of a poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: In UNI the N is replaced by RAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Urari is a variant of curare, the South American arrow poison, so it is where the poisoning comes from.

clue.text: Two seconds to net the French fish

indicators.note: netting something catches it inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: MO, a moment or second, plus S, the abbreviation for second
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A French fish is caught within two seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Mola is the ocean sunfish genus, a huge flattened sea fish, so its plural names several of them.

clue.text: US composer is hearing soprano

blocks.note: a sitting of a court or committee to hear a case
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: An American composer is listening to a soprano sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like listening but is a court sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Sessions was a twentieth-century American composer of symphonies and the opera Montezuma.

clue.text: Blacken associate overlooking most of the former Zulu movement

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking over means standing above, so the first pieces sit on top
most of means nearly all, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: to blacken with ink
A is the abbreviation for associate
that, as in 'this and that', minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A smear campaign against a colleague ignores an old Zulu political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkatha was a Zulu cultural and political organisation in South Africa, later the Inkatha Freedom Party.

clue.text: Gadflies odd in set so fixed

indicators.note: one word placed in the next means it sits within those letters
something fixed in the sense of rigged has been tampered with and rearranged

blocks.note: rum is British slang for strange
taken as written

explanation.surface: Biting insects behave oddly in a fixed set.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM goes inside an anagram of SET SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrum is an old word for the oestrus, a botfly or gadfly, and also for a sting or frenzy.

clue.text: Spectator first to report the boundaries of Stokes? Possibly

definitions.text: Spectator first to report the boundaries of Stokes? Possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the gathered letters are mixed
the first to do something leads, so only the opening letter is taken
boundaries are edges, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter
its two end letters

explanation.surface: A cricket watcher is the first to report Ben Stokes hitting boundaries, as a commentator might.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Stokes is an England cricket captain; a boundary in cricket is a shot reaching the rope. The whole clue describes a commentator.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportscaster is a broadcaster who describes games live, watching like a spectator and reporting the action.

clue.text: Real loss surprisingly makes you happy!

indicators.note: a surprising turn means things are not as expected, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ironic claim that a genuine bereavement leaves you cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: If everything is roses, life is pleasant and untroubled, an idiom for a contented state.

clue.text: Wee children finally repelled by vegetable in Scotland

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter is used
being repelled means being driven back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: both are words for urine
its final letter

explanation.surface: Little children are put off by a Scottish vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like Scots for small but is urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is the Scots word for a turnip or swede, served with haggis on Burns Night.

clue.text: High-up person perhaps goes white in state requiring aid endlessly

indicators.note: one piece placed in another means it sits inside it
without an end means the last letter is chopped

blocks.note: turns pale
need, a condition of wanting help, missing its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone at altitude blanches in a state needing help.
explanation.walkthrough: Nepal holds the Himalayas, so its people live high up; 'state' is a condition, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Nepal lives among the highest mountains on Earth, so 'high-up person' is a playful example.

clue.text: Rake around greens daily

indicators.note: one word placed around the next encloses it

blocks.note: a roué is a dissolute man
greens is slang for money, as is tin

explanation.surface: Raking the golf greens is a daily chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' and 'greens' suggest gardening or golf, but a rake is a libertine and greens are money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every day as a matter of course is routine, the adjective meaning regular and habitual.

clue.text: Shoe tie coming from side street going west

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west is moving right to left, against the reading direction

blocks.note: a side in a dispute or a role
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A shoelace has come from a side street heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-strap is a shoe fastening shaped like a T, a strap tying the shoe across the instep.

clue.text: Brown surrounding President’s seal

indicators.note: a word surrounding another has that other word inside it

blocks.note: to sear is to brown meat quickly
Abe, Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A brown President's official seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' looks like a stamp of office but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea bear is a name for the fur seal, a large-eared seal hunted for its dense pelt.

clue.text: Part of motor turns around, expending energy

indicators.note: turned around means facing back, so the letters are read backwards
expending something uses it up, so that letter goes

blocks.note: spins
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Part of a motor turns around, using up energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: The stator is the stationary part of an electric motor or generator, within which the rotor spins.

clue.text: Moll with tarts? Refuse to go up inside

definitions.note: the surname that goes with Moll in the Defoe title

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom to the top
something put inside another is held within it

blocks.note: open pastry cases
red is a dialect word for rubbish

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend with loose women, as rubbish rises inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Moll Flanders is Daniel Defoe's 1722 novel about a thief and prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's heroine is Moll Flanders, so the surname is what accompanies Moll in her full name.

clue.text: One police boss is a user

blocks.note: a, meaning one
head of the CID, the British detective branch

explanation.surface: A senior detective is secretly taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidhead is a habitual taker of LSD, and user is slang for a drug addict.

clue.text: Walk pompously in support

blocks.note: first meaning: swagger
second meaning: a brace or bar in a framework

explanation.surface: Someone parades self-importantly while wearing a brace.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to swagger, and the noun is a rod bearing a load in a building or aircraft frame.

clue.text: Mix of ingredients still perhaps in smart room

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: an elegant reception room
a still is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: A mixture of ingredients still sits in an elegant room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' seems to be an adverb, but it is a noun, a single film frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A salpicon is a mixture of diced meat, fish or vegetables bound in a sauce, used as a filling.

clue.text: Stirs up trouble for pedants

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters before it are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone causes a fuss for pedantic people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirs up trouble' reads as one phrase; 'trouble' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Purists insist on strict correctness in language or style, as pedants do.

clue.text: See friend behind pub with cocaine and sort of acid

indicators.note: coming behind another word places it straight after it

blocks.note: the letter whose name is said 'see'
a tavern
French for friend
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: You see a friend behind the pub taking cocaine and some sort of acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamic acid is a compound found in cinnamon oil, used in flavourings and perfumes.

clue.text: Old-fashioned praise surrounds new King

indicators.note: a word that surrounds another holds it inside

blocks.note: hery is an archaic Spenserian verb meaning to praise
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned praise is lavished on a new monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry is the name of eight English kings, so it stands for a king by example.

clue.text: Rural Dean ignored by unpleasant person: that’s enough for Will

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: RD is the abbreviation for Rural Dean
a rude word for a nasty person

explanation.surface: A clergyman is snubbed by a nasty man, who says he has had enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Will is Shakespeare, who uses the Italian word in The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Basta is Italian for stop or no more, an interjection Shakespeare uses, so it is his way of calling a halt.

clue.text: Sign that’s found in Roman art

indicators.note: what is found in something lies inside it

blocks.note: ars is the Latin word for art
i.e., id est, that is

explanation.surface: A zodiac sign appears in Roman artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a hidden word in 'Roman art', but no sign is spelt there; ars is the Latin for art.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: What is hard in a salad?

definitions.text: What is hard in a salad?

indicators.note: a salad is a jumble of mixed items, so these letters are tossed together

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question asking which salad ingredient is the crunchy one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and the words 'is hard' supply its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a firm, crisp root eaten raw in salads, the crunchy element among soft leaves.

clue.text: Religious teachers in pub nearby, half-cut

indicators.note: cut in half means only one half of the word is kept

blocks.note: a bar
beside, keeping its first half

explanation.surface: Preachers in a nearby pub are half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for tipsy, but here it means half of a word is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbe was a Waldensian pastor or preacher, so the plural names those religious teachers.

clue.text: A payment covers one cordial drink

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps around it

blocks.note: per, as in so much a head
scot is an old tax or payment, as in scot-free
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A fee includes one soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' means 'for each', as in a pound a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Persicot is a liqueur made from peaches or apricot kernels steeped in spirit, a cordial.

clue.text: Pole said to be in a tangle

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an oar is a pole for rowing

explanation.surface: A rowing pole gets caught up in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tangle is a kind of seaweed, not a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore, or ware, is a dialect name for seaweed, and tangle is the name for kelp seaweed.

clue.text: Place devoted to the Virgin Mary is forgotten

indicators.note: the forgotten word is left out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a Marist belongs to the Society of Mary
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shrine to the Virgin Mary has been neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: A mart is a market or trading place, so it is a place of commerce.

clue.text: Standard rent mentioned for theatre pit

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so this word is given by its sound

blocks.note: the norm, as in golf
a rent is a rip

explanation.surface: The usual rent is quoted for seats in the theatre pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid but is a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: In American theatres the parterre is the rear stalls area of the ground floor, the old pit.

clue.text: Expert went by old lady screening sun

indicators.note: a screen stands around something and hides it within

blocks.note: went past
Latin for mother, old slang for one's mum
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A skilled person walked past an old woman shading herself from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside MATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is someone thoroughly skilled; 'passed master' is the variant spelling recorded in Chambers.
